title: Prune v0 config artifacts, migrate feature flags, and sunset legacy admin APIs
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Scope: Remove legacy v0 configuration bundles and admin endpoints that remain in the codebase and runtime routing layer. Migrate remaining customers/flags using the old config schema to the normalized configv1 schema and flags_v2. Sunset endpoints under /admin/v0/* and the rollout webhook /rollout/v0/notify after migration.

Motivation: Several internal services still read or reference v0 config blobs and legacy admin endpoints. These create maintenance overhead, prevent kernel selection simplifications, and block further refactors to the routing layer. Cleaning them up reduces surface area for errors, simplifies rollout code paths, and reduces memory overhead caused by legacy parsing.

Outcomes we expect:
- Remove ~3k lines of compatibility parsing and the v0 schema loader.
- Remove 4 legacy admin HTTP endpoints and one webhook receiver.
- Migrate all active feature flags from legacy_toggle_* to flags_v2 with explicit typed schema.
- Reduce config-parsing CPU time for cold-starts by ~8-12% (measure in perf dashboard).

Plan (phased):
1) Inventory (DONE) – discover all services, routes, cron jobs, and customer configs referencing v0 artifacts. List is in the linked spreadsheet.
2) Compatibility shim (IN PROGRESS) – implement a short-lived runtime shim that translates v0 -> configv1 in-memory for requests that still send v0 payloads. This is behind an opt-in feature flag (ENG-14521.compat-shim).
3) Flag migration script – write idempotent migration script that reads feature flag rows from the legacy store and writes them to flags_v2 with tracers to allow audit.
4) Deprecation window & telemetry – emit deprecation headers and create dashboard panels to track requests touching v0 endpoints and shim hits.
5) Canary & rollout – enable removal in canary region for non-critical routes, validate for 72h, then expand to all regions.
6) Hard remove – once shim hit rate is 0 and all customers migrated, delete the shim code, remove route handlers, and prune DB schema related to v0.
7) Post-mortem & follow-ups – verify no regressions, cleanup leftover envvars, and close parent tickets.

Testing and verification:
- Unit tests for migration idempotency and rollback behavior.
- Integration tests that simulate old clients calling /admin/v0/* and verify shim path.
- Load test that compares cold-start parsing latency before and after removal.
- Canary telemetry: shim_hits, shim_miss, config_migration_success, admin_v0_403_count.

Rollback strategy:
- If high error rates appear during canary, re-enable shim via runtime flag and route traffic back to prior service version. Migration steps are reversible (migration script writes a migration marker; we will keep source rows until post-hard-remove).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Hidden consumers (internal scripts, on-prem deployments) still call v0 endpoints. Mitigation: Send deprecation notices via internal mailing lists and create a temporary compatibility layer that logs callers and returns a helpful error payload.
- Risk: Edge-case flags with non-standard values. Mitigation: Migration script will create an exceptions log and route those cases to Manual Review queue owned by Feature Flags team.

Runbook snippets (to be copied to oncall doc):
- If rollout webhook /rollout/v0/notify fails after removal, re-enable shim by flipping ENG-14521.compat-shim to true and revert gateway rules for rollout webhook.
- If migrations partially fail, inspect migration_errors table and re-run script with --resume. Contact Diego and PM for manual fixes.

Acceptance criteria (before closing):
- shim_hit_rate == 0 for 7 days and no critical regressions in logs.
- No services reference v0 parsers in repo (grep across monorepo).
- DB tables/columns for v0 are scheduled for drop and marked in schema migration plan.
- Post-cleanup perf dashboard shows expected improvement.

Notes on backward compatibility decisions:
We prefer a short-lived in-memory shim rather than a long-lived API compatibility layer to reduce long-term complexity. The shim intentionally logs any callers with a 1-week TTL to allow outreach. Customer-facing docs will include migration steps and sample curl commands to exercise flags_v2.
